prompt.context: A tire manufacturer in Vietnam, VieTire, has been the only player in that market due to high tariffs on imports. They dominate the tire industry. As it stands, the tariff is 50% of the total cost to produce and ship a tire to Vietnam. Because of the forces of globalization and lower consumer prices, the Vietnamese government decided to lower the tariff by 5% a year for the next ten years. VieTire is very concerned about this change, as it will radically alter the landscape of the industry in Vietnam.
prompt.question: They hire you to assess the situation and advise them on what steps to take.

clarifying_info.q: What are the major costs associated with making a tire at VieTire?
clarifying_info.a: Raw materials comprise about 20% of the cost, labor 40%, and all other costs such as overhead 40%. The average tire costs about $40 to make.

clarifying_info.q: Why is labor such a high cost for VieTire?
clarifying_info.a: Things are done more manually. Most of the technological advances in the industry have not yet been implemented in Vietnam.

clarifying_info.q: What does a foreign competitor's tire cost to produce?
clarifying_info.a: An average tire manufacturer in the US produces tires at a cost of $30 each.

clarifying_info.q: What is the shipping cost to bring a tire from the US to Vietnam?

framework: Understand the current cost structure of VieTire's product
Determine the impending competitive situation (when will foreign players enter?)
Calculate the impact the tariff reduction will have year by year
Recommend specific steps VieTire can take to protect itself from increased competition

questions.prompt: What is the current all-in cost of a domestically produced VieTire tire vs. an imported tire?
questions.guidance: VieTire produces at $40/tire. An imported US tire costs $30 to produce + $4 shipping = $34 before tariff. With a 50% tariff on the $34 landed cost, total imported cost = $34 × 1.50 = $51. So VieTire ($40) is cheaper than the imported tire ($51) today, protecting the market.

math.setup: US production cost $30 + shipping $4 = $34 base landed cost. Tariff = 50% of $34 = $17. Total imported cost = $34 + $17 = $51.
steps: Imported cost ($51) > VieTire cost ($40): foreign competitors will not enter today
math.answer: Imported tire costs $51 today vs. VieTire's $40; no competitive threat under current tariff.

questions.prompt: Model the year-by-year cost of imported tires as the tariff drops 5 percentage points per year. When does competition become a threat?
questions.guidance: Apply the declining tariff rate to the $34 base landed cost each year. Competition begins to consider entry around year 4 (when imported cost ~$43) and will surely enter by year 6 (when imported cost ~$39.60, below VieTire's $40). Also note that improving technology could lower US production costs further, accelerating entry.

math.setup: Each year tariff drops 5 pp. Imported cost = $34 × (1 + tariff rate). VieTire domestic cost assumed constant at $40.
steps: Year 4: 30% → $34 × 1.30 = $44.20 — Consideration of entrance if willing to take a price cut
Year 6: 20% → $34 × 1.20 = $40.80 — Entered the market (approximately at parity or below)
math.answer: Foreign competitors will start seriously considering entry around year 4 and will effectively enter by year 6, when their all-in cost drops below or approaches VieTire's $40 production cost. Note: the casebook table uses slightly different rounding ($47.90, $46.00, etc.) but the conclusion is the same.

brainstorming.prompt: What specific steps should VieTire take to protect themselves from increasing competition over the next 4-6 years?

categories.name: Cost Reduction / Operations
ideas: Benchmark against world-class tire manufacturers and reengineer production methods
Invest in the latest manufacturing technology to reduce labor intensity
Automate manual processes to bring labor cost closer to global norms
Optimize supply chain and raw material sourcing to reduce the 20% materials cost

categories.name: Workforce / Labor
ideas: Increase the skills of labor to improve output quality and productivity
Contain hourly wages while raising productivity through training
Explore partnerships with technical schools to build a skilled workforce pipeline

categories.name: Customer / Market
ideas: Develop customer loyalty programs to lock in a base of market share
Build brand equity as the trusted domestic player
Offer guarantees or service networks that foreign entrants cannot easily replicate
Price competitively now to pre-empt foreign entry

categories.name: Strategic Positioning
ideas: Explore government lobbying to slow or reverse further tariff reductions
Consider forming joint ventures or licensing deals with foreign manufacturers to access technology
Evaluate expansion into lower-cost production regions within Vietnam
Diversify into adjacent automotive components to reduce dependence on tires

recommendation: VieTire has approximately 4-6 years before foreign competition becomes a serious threat. It must use this window to close the cost gap by investing in technology and process reengineering to drive unit production cost materially below $40.
Simultaneously, VieTire should build customer loyalty and brand equity so that price parity alone does not erode market share when imports arrive.
risks: Technology costs of the upgrade investment could be substantial and may require external financing
Foreign manufacturers may reduce their own production costs faster than modeled, compressing the timeline
Labor restructuring could cause workforce disruption or labor unrest
Loyalty programs may not be sufficient if price differential becomes large enough
next_steps: Commission a detailed benchmarking study against leading US and Asian tire manufacturers to identify specific cost-reduction opportunities
Develop a capital investment plan and timeline for upgrading manufacturing equipment
Design and launch a customer loyalty and distribution-lock-in program within the next 12 months
Establish a regulatory affairs team to monitor and engage with Vietnamese trade policy
